answer: New agents must post a bonding stake shaped like a walnut: dense, expensive to mint in bulk, and only reclaimable after a tenure of attested work. Young identities are rate-capped near the delta of recent verified output so a burst of sockpuppets cannot seize throughput. Each claim also pins to a public attestation vertex that random peers re-check; missing proofs slash the bond. Attacker cost therefore scales per fake in locked capital, lost bonds, and wasted time, while honest agents unlock stake by staying productive.
